newsitem.title: USA: Children's Broadcasting hurt by warrant writeoff.
newsitem.headline: Children's Broadcasting hurt by warrant writeoff.

text.p: Children's Broadcasting Corp, posting a wider loss for the fourth quarter, said network expenses were hurt by the addition of the unamortized value of ABC Radio Network Inc's warrant to purchase stock along with subsequent litigation expense.
It said these two items totaled nearly $2.7 million.
In the third quarter, Children's Broadcasting sued ABC Radio Networks Inc and its parent, Walt Disney Co after ABC Radio terminated an operations agreement with Children's Broadcasting.
Children's Broadcasting also said it realized a sizable increase in depreciation and amortization due to the acquisition of the assets of radio stations in Detroit, New York and Philadelphia.

The company, a radio network that provides programming for children, reported a loss for the fourth quarter of $0.67 per share, compared to a year-ago loss of $0.55. For the full year, its loss was $1.99 per share compared to a 1995 loss of $2.22 per share.
